children: Super Micro Computer is caught up in a Department of Justice probe into Alice Huang, the suspected Chinese intelligence asset with whom Nvidia's ousted CEO Jensen Huang had an affair, according to a report.

The agency is investigating whether entities linked to Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based data-center company Megaspeed, were involved in efforts to smuggle Super Micro products into China, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. The U.S. Attorney's Office in Manhattan is leading the probe.

"Supermicro has been responsive to inquiries and has fully cooperated with U.S. and Taiwanese officials, while also voluntarily providing information and engaging with all requests from Singapore authorities to date," the company said in a statement Thursday. "Megaspeed is not, and has never been, a Super Micro customer."
Super Micro stock tumbled 12% on Thursday. The server maker was one of several names already struggling because of its links to Nvidia and the broader artificial-intelligence buildout.

The reported investigation threatens to reignite the firestorm Super Micro faced starting in March, when the U.S. government charged co-founder Yih-Shyan "Wally" Liaw and two other individuals for an alleged scheme to divert Super Micro servers to China in a violation of U.S. export controls. Liaw immediately resigned.

A few months later, Taiwanese investigators raided Super Micro's office and several other sites in Taiwan as part of a broader probe into how restricted Nvidia chips had allegedly made their way to Asia.
Super Micro said in August that it had completed an internal investigation led by independent board members regarding the March indictments.

The investigation didn't find evidence that current members of senior management had knowledge of the alleged scheme or of any actual diversion of restricted hardware, Super Micro said at the time. The company added that it had implemented recommended enhancements to its export compliance program and was cooperating with authorities.
The U.S. Attorney's Office, and the Justice Department didn't immediately respond to Barron's requests for comment.

A fresh investigation could be positive news for Dell, one of Super Micro's chief competitors in AI servers that incorporate Nvidia hardware. Dell stock has soared roughly 200% this year on the back of enormous AI equipment spending, and it recovered from a sharp fall on Thursday morning to rise 0.9%.
